microtheory.name: information_theory_coding
microtheory.definition: Shannon's information theory + coding theory. The mathematical framework for measuring + transmitting + compressing information. Entropy, mutual information, channel capacity, source coding, channel coding, rate-distortion, lossy/lossless compression, error correction, codec design. Directly grounds Paper 1's Axiom 2 (Serialisation adequacy): the claim that codec pairs (W_j, W_j^{-1}) preserve task-relevant content up to ε is exactly the rate-distortion question. The substrate's W_j is a source code; its ε is the rate-distortion bound; codec adequacy = operating point on the rate-distortion curve.

concepts.name: information_shannon
concepts.definition: Shannon 1948. Quantified information as -log p(x). Founding of the field. Substrate analogue: Jabberwock's substrate operates over information so quantified.

concepts.name: entropy_shannon
concepts.definition: H(X) = -Σ p(x) log p(x). Average information content. Lower = more predictable. Bits when log base 2. Substrate analogue: substrate's compression objective's target.

concepts.name: self_information
concepts.definition: Rare events carry more information. I(x) = -log p(x). Surprising events have high self-information. Substrate analogue: substrate's surprise / ΔF.

concepts.name: joint_entropy
concepts.definition: H(X,Y) = -Σ p(x,y) log p(x,y). Information in pair. Substrate analogue: substrate's compound state.

concepts.name: conditional_entropy
concepts.definition: H(Y|X) = H(X,Y) - H(X). Information in Y given X. Substrate analogue: substrate's conditional uncertainty.

concepts.name: mutual_information
concepts.definition: I(X;Y) = H(X) + H(Y) - H(X,Y). Information X contains about Y. Symmetric. Substrate analogue: substrate's cross-Mt informational coupling.

concepts.name: kl_divergence
concepts.definition: D_KL(P||Q) = Σ p log(p/q). Information lost when Q approximates P. Asymmetric. Substrate analogue: substrate's belief-update cost.

concepts.name: cross_entropy
concepts.definition: H(P,Q) = -Σ p log q. Used in ML losses. = H(P) + D_KL(P||Q). Substrate analogue: substrate's prediction error.

concepts.name: source_coding
concepts.definition: Shannon's source coding theorem. Compressible to H(X) bits per symbol on average. Substrate analogue: substrate's representational compression.

concepts.name: huffman_coding
concepts.definition: Optimal prefix code for known symbol distribution. Variable length. Substrate analogue: substrate's frequency-adapted symbol encoding.

concepts.name: arithmetic_coding
concepts.definition: Encodes whole message as single number in [0,1). Beats Huffman's per-symbol overhead. Substrate analogue: substrate's continuous compression.

concepts.name: lossless_compression
concepts.definition: Exact reconstruction. Limited by entropy. ZIP, gzip, FLAC. Substrate analogue: substrate's exact-recovery storage.

concepts.name: minimum_description_length
concepts.definition: MDL. Rissanen. Best model is shortest combined description of model + data given model. Substrate analogue: substrate's parsimony drive.

concepts.name: channel_capacity
concepts.definition: Shannon's channel coding theorem. Maximum rate of reliable transmission. C = max_p I(X;Y). Substrate analogue: substrate's per-channel info bandwidth.

concepts.name: noisy_channel_theorem
concepts.definition: Below capacity: arbitrarily low error rate achievable. Above: error rate bounded away from zero. Substrate analogue: substrate's reliability vs throughput tradeoff.

concepts.name: error_correction_code
concepts.definition: Adds redundancy enabling error detection + correction. Hamming, Reed-Solomon, LDPC, Turbo, Polar. Substrate analogue: substrate's redundancy-for-reliability.

concepts.name: hamming_distance
concepts.definition: Number of positions where two codewords differ. d_min sets correction capability. Substrate analogue: substrate's discrimination metric.

concepts.name: rate_distortion_theory
concepts.definition: Berger 1971. R(D) = min I(X; X̂) subject to E[d(X,X̂)] ≤ D. Quantifies optimal lossy compression. THE FRAMEWORK FOR PAPER 1'S AXIOM 2: codec pair (W_j, W_j^{-1}) preserves content up to ε IS the rate-distortion question. Substrate analogue: substrate's task-relevant-content preservation under serialisation.

concepts.name: rate_distortion_function
concepts.definition: R(D) — minimum rate to achieve distortion D. Convex, decreasing. R(0) = H(X) (lossless); R(∞) = 0. Substrate analogue: substrate's ε-vs-bitrate tradeoff curve.

concepts.name: distortion_measure
concepts.definition: d(x, x̂) — cost of representing x as x̂. Squared error, Hamming, perceptual. Substrate analogue: substrate's task-relevance distortion.

concepts.name: lossy_compression
concepts.definition: Discards information to achieve lower rate. JPEG, MP3, h.264. Operates on rate-distortion curve. Substrate analogue: substrate's perceptual-relevant retention.

concepts.name: perceptual_coding
concepts.definition: Exploits limits of human perception (masking, JND) to discard inaudible/invisible info. MP3, AAC, Opus. Substrate analogue: substrate's perceptual-validity coding.

concepts.name: codec_definition
concepts.definition: Coder + decoder pair. CODer-DECoder. Substrate analogue: substrate's W_j + W_j^{-1} pair (Paper 1 Axiom 2).

concepts.name: codec_pair_adequacy
concepts.definition: A codec pair is adequate for a content class iff it preserves task-relevant content up to ε across that class. EXACTLY Paper 1's Axiom 2 framing. Substrate analogue: substrate's codec adequacy test.

concepts.name: epsilon_distortion_bound
concepts.definition: The ε in 'preserves up to ε'. Task-relevant content distortion bound. Depends on content class + codec choice + intended use. Substrate analogue: substrate's tolerance parameter.

concepts.name: lossy_round_trip
concepts.definition: X → W(X) → W^{-1}(W(X)) ≠ X in general. Loss = d(X, W^{-1}(W(X))). Adequacy: loss ≤ ε. Substrate analogue: substrate's serialise-then-deserialise distortion.

concepts.name: sampling_theorem
concepts.definition: Shannon-Whittaker-Nyquist. Bandlimited signal recoverable from samples at 2× max frequency. Substrate analogue: substrate's sampling adequacy.

concepts.name: nyquist_shannon
concepts.definition: Sample rate ≥ 2 × bandwidth → perfect reconstruction. Substrate analogue: substrate's discretization bound.

concepts.name: quantization_noise
concepts.definition: Loss from amplitude discretization. ~Δ²/12 variance for uniform quantizer. Substrate analogue: substrate's discretization error.

concepts.name: channel_coding_separation
concepts.definition: Shannon. Source coding + channel coding can be designed independently with no rate penalty. Substrate analogue: substrate's compression + reliability separability.

concepts.name: data_processing_inequality
concepts.definition: Processing cannot increase information. I(X; f(Y)) ≤ I(X; Y). Substrate analogue: substrate's downstream-cannot-recover-lost-info.

concepts.name: fanos_inequality
concepts.definition: Lower bound on error probability given conditional entropy. Substrate analogue: substrate's reconstruction error lower bound.

rules.name: serialisation_adequacy_is_rate_distortion
rules.head: Jabberwock encounters Paper 1's Axiom 2 (Serialisation adequacy)
rules.body: the axiom IS the rate-distortion framing: codec pair preserves content up to ε corresponds to operating at distortion ε on the rate-distortion curve. Information theory provides the formal grounding.

rules.name: lossy_round_trip_bounds_loss_not_eliminates_it
rules.head: Jabberwock processes input X via serialisation + deserialisation
rules.body: the round-trip is not exact (Shannon source coding for lossy compression). Loss is bounded by ε, not eliminated. Paper 1's Axiom 2 echoes this: 'serialisation is lossy; the claim is that well-chosen codecs bound the loss, not that an exact inverse exists'.

rules.name: data_processing_inequality_limits_recovery
rules.head: Jabberwock processes information downstream of a serialisation
rules.body: no downstream processing can recover information lost in the codec. Data processing inequality. Substrate's downstream limit.

rules.name: kl_divergence_measures_belief_update_cost
rules.head: Jabberwock updates beliefs from P to Q
rules.body: the information cost is D_KL(P||Q) bits. Substrate's belief-update efficiency metric.

rules.name: mdl_grounds_parsimony_drive
rules.head: Jabberwock's parsimony drive selects compressed representations
rules.body: Rissanen's MDL principle formalises this: best model is shortest description of model + data given model. Substrate's parsimony drive = MDL.
